diagnostic_evidence.quote: for  any $ \bw\in {\cal S}$, let $d(\bw)$ be the minimum of  \eqref{eq:dual}
for  any $ \bw\in {\cal S}$ with at least $n+1$ nonzero $w_j$'s

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma is stated for every w in S, but when w has fewer than n+1 positive entries the matrix B = sqrt(W)[0,C_q]N has a nontrivial kernel, and (for k <= n+1-l positive weights) one can choose c with both Bc=0 and Ac=0 (pick [c_1;c_3] in the kernel of the k x (n+1) Cauchy submatrix and solve the k equations C_{p,1}c_1 + C_{p,2}c_2 = 0 for c_2). The pencil (A^H A, B^H B) is then singular and 'the smallest eigenvalue' and its eigenpair are not well defined, so the asserted characterization does not hold as stated; only the PSD conclusion A^H A - d B^H B >= 0 survives in general. The Proposition that follows correctly restricts to at least n+1 nonzero weights, while the Lemma does not.

failure_location.quote: Then  $(d(\bw),\bc(\bw))$ is the eigenpair associated with the smallest eigenvalue of the generalized eigenvalue problem $A^{\HH}A\bc(\bw)=d(\bw)B^{\HH}B\bc(\bw)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the eigenpair statement to w with at least n+1 nonzero entries (so B has full column rank and the pencil is regular), or phrase it as the smallest finite eigenvalue of the PSD pencil, while keeping the PSD conclusion for all w in S via the direct scaling argument.
issues.overall_effect: The eigenpair characterization in Lemma lem:KKT is unreliable for weight vectors with fewer than n+1 positive entries; the positive semidefiniteness conclusion (the only part used in Theorem thm:strongdualityRuttan) remains valid, so downstream results are unaffected.
issues.title: Lemma on dual-function optimality asserts an eigenpair of a possibly singular pencil for every w in S
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis restriction or rephrasing fixes the statement; the part of the lemma actually used later (positive semidefiniteness) is valid for all w, so no dependent result or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: First, by Theorem \ref{lem:baryrational2}, we know that both the best approximation $\xi^*=p^*/q^*\in \scrR_{(n)}$  of \eqref{eq:bestf}, and the corresponding   $\wtd \xi=\wtd p/\wtd q$ in barycentric formula achieving the minimum $d(\bw)$ can be parameterized by \eqref{eq:baryform}.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is for general 0 <= l <= n+1 and the dual d(w) is built on the interpolation-constrained parameterization, yet eta_infty is defined as the error of a solution of the unconstrained problem (eq:bestf). The unconstrained minimax error can be strictly smaller than every d(w) (e.g., f exactly rational of type n with inconsistent interpolation values gives eta_infty = 0 while d(w) > 0), so the inequality max d(w) <= eta_infty^2 is false as written. The proof only works when xi^* solves the constrained problem (eq:baryInterpMinmax), since Theorem lem:baryrational2 is invoked to write xi^* in the form (eq:baryform), which requires xi^*(t_j)=y_j.
